name: Iota Persei
description: A naked-eye star 10.5 parsecs away, 1.4 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the CHARA Array.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 19373: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.246 +/- 0.008 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.412 +/- 0.009

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 19373: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.169 +/- 0.013

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 19373: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 5915 +/- 29

distance.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 19373: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 94.87 +/- 0.23 mas, inverted

color.disagreement: Not explained. The Kharitonov colour differs from the Pulkovo colour by 14 levels in one channel, 2 over the agreement threshold. Both are ground spectrophotometry of the same star; the Pulkovo colour is used because that catalogue comes first in the route order.

text.card: A naked-eye star 11 parsecs away whose disc the CHARA Array measured: 1.4 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.246 milliarcseconds, which gives 1.412 solar radii and 5,915 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 5 and 10, HD 19373: limb-darkened diameter, R, Teff
